Your branch feature/demo has a clean worktree and an existing commit. Its cached upstream shows it ahead, but the current remote state is unknown, so readiness is provisional. To confirm, I would run:

    git fetch --no-tags origin
    git rev-list --left-right --count origin/feature/demo...HEAD
    git log --oneline origin/feature/demo..HEAD

Fetch updates local remote-tracking information and downloads objects; it does not publish commits. The count shows remote-only commits first and local-only commits second. Zero remote-only commits with local commits ahead supports a fast-forward publication; divergence requires review. The log identifies commits that would be published.

No push or push dry run is needed, so the pre-push hook and its marker remain untouched. Publishing is not authorized, and I would stop after reporting the results.
